interest: Covers rumors of Japanese sounding operations and the mystery trawler Santa Marta in the Gulf of Fonseca.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.20215) comprises diplomatic instructions, consular despatches, naval intelligence reports, telegrams, newspaper clippings, and cross-reference sheets dating from 1932 to 1938 concerning suspected Japanese military, naval, and espionage activities in Honduras and surrounding Central American waters. Originating from an early 1932 Office of Naval Intelligence warning regarding Japanese nationals conducting covert topographical surveys under the guise of fishermen, the file records extensive investigations by American Minister Julius G. Lay, Marine Corps Attaché Major H. S. Fassett, and consular officials along the Pacific and Caribbean coasts. The records document local alarms and Salvadoran military alerts over unidentified, unlighted vessels making nocturnal incursions into the Gulf of Fonseca to take soundings, as well as subsequent surveillance of visiting Japanese commercial travelers, including industrial exhibition promoter Kurow Itoh, textile representative Jumpei Yoden, and trade envoy Y. Megurikami, culminating in reports of Japanese proposals to establish agricultural colonies for growing strategic crops like cotton and castor beans.

subfiles.about: Instruction from the Department of State directing the American Minister in Honduras to discreetly investigate reports of Japanese nationals conducting coastal surveys disguised as fishermen.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 231 directs Minister Julius Lay to investigate reports of Japanese posing as fishermen conducting coastal surveys in Honduras, with identical orders sent across Central America and northern South America.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 231 to Julius G. Lay on Investigating Japanese Coastal Surveys

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting initial investigative measures undertaken by U.S. consular officers and the Naval Attaché regarding reported Japanese activities in Honduras and El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 406: Lay reports confidential directives to Honduran consuls, Naval Attaché Fassett's planned Gulf of Fonseca inspection, and the interrogation of two Japanese nationals in El Salvador.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 406 from Julius G. Lay on Preliminary Inquiries into Japanese Presence

subfiles.about: Spanish-language newspaper clipping reporting the arrival of two mysterious Japanese travelers at the port of La Libertad in El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: El Cronista (Tegucigalpa) reports the February 1932 arrival at La Libertad of Japanese couple Kinmujo Siraki and Juichi Honke, questioned by San Salvador police.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 406: Spanish Clipping from El Cronista

subfiles.about: English translation of the newspaper article from El Cronista concerning the arrival and police questioning of two Japanese travelers in El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: English translation of the El Cronista article: Kinmujo Siraki and wife Juichi Honke arrived at La Libertad and were ordered to present identification in San Salvador.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 406: Translation of El Cronista Article

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting that investigations by the Naval Attaché and consular officers found no evidence of Japanese naval or fishing activities in Honduran waters.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 424: Lay reports rumors of Japanese activity in Honduran waters are unfounded; Fassett's coastal inspection and consular inquiries found nothing suspicious.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 424 from Julius G. Lay Refuting Japanese Activities in Honduran Waters

subfiles.about: Naval Attaché report detailing field investigations into alleged Japanese and foreign maritime activities along the coasts of Honduras.
subfiles.summary: Major Fassett's ONI report finds no evidence of Japanese boats on Honduras's coasts; local fishing uses only dugout canoes, making foreign craft easily noticeable.
subfiles.title: ONI Attaché Report No. 25-32 by Major H. S. Fassett on Coastal Investigations

subfiles.about: Confidential telegram reporting press allegations that a mysterious San Francisco-registered fishing boat was conducting nocturnal hydrographic soundings for Japan in the Gulf of Fonseca.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 43: Lay reports a mysterious vessel, registered in San Francisco as a fishing boat, making nighttime runs into the Gulf of Fonseca, suspected of Japanese hydrographic soundings.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 43 from Julius G. Lay on Suspicious Vessel in Gulf of Fonseca

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting findings from the Salvadoran Ministry of War regarding the unidentified vessel operating in the Gulf of Fonseca.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 13: McCafferty reports Salvadoran officials could not identify the lightless, flagless vessel in the Gulf of Fonseca, which had departed northward two days earlier.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 13 from William J. McCafferty on Suspicious Boat in Gulf of Fonseca

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a translated newspaper report on the nocturnal movements of an alleged Japanese espionage vessel in the Gulf of Fonseca.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 901: Lay transmits an El Cronista article on the Gulf of Fonseca mystery ship and reports a discreet Legation investigation into its suspected Japanese ties.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 901 from Julius G. Lay Transmitting El Cronista Article on Gulf Mystery Ship

subfiles.about: English translation of an article from El Cronista asserting that a mysterious San Francisco fishing vessel is gathering naval intelligence in the Gulf of Fonseca for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Translated article describing a mystery boat's nighttime incursions into the Gulf of Fonseca, suspected of Japanese espionage and hydrographic surveying for Japan's war ministries.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 901: Translation of El Cronista Article on Mystery Ship

subfiles.about: Despatch providing physical descriptions and operational details of the unidentified vessel operating in Central American Pacific waters.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 904: Lay describes the mystery ship as a 150-foot white vessel that fled aerial observation off Guatemala; Salvadoran forces lacked patrol boats to intercept it.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 904 from Julius G. Lay on Description and Movements of Suspicious Vessel

subfiles.about: Despatch identifying the suspicious vessel in the Gulf of Fonseca as the Santa Marta of San Francisco and detailing local security precautions.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 908: Lay identifies the mystery craft as the Santa Marta of San Francisco, a fast vessel suspected of contraband running that had previously visited the Panama Canal Zone.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 908 from Julius G. Lay Identifying Mystery Ship as the Santa Marta

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the arrival in Honduras of Japanese national Kurow Itoh and assessing potential ulterior motives concerning Panama Canal security.
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Hoffmann reports Kurow Itoh's arrival in Honduras claiming to promote Japan's 1937 Nagoya Industrial Exhibition, suspecting his real motives given negligible Honduran commercial interest in it.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Walter W. Hoffmann on the Presence in Honduras of Kurow Itoh

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a despatch regarding Japanese efforts to alter Honduran tariff laws and the commercial mission of Y. Megurikami.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Despatch 217: Japan sought tariff-law changes in Honduras, with Y. Megurikami negotiating a draft commercial agreement.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 217 regarding Y. Megurikami and Tariff Modification

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing reports on the suspicious business activities of Jumpei Yoden and Y. Megurikami in Tegucigalpa.
subfiles.summary: Schuler's memo on Jumpei Yoden, suspected of ties to Japanese promoter Y. Megurikami; concludes no departmental action is required.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Activities of Jumpei Yoden

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on suspicions raised by a local American banker regarding Japanese commercial representative Jumpei Yoden.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 319: Erwin relays suspicions about Jumpei Yoden of H. Nishizawa Shoten, seen frequently with trade envoy Megurikami while claiming to collect debts in Tegucigalpa.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 319 from John D. Erwin on the Activities of Jumpei Yoden

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a despatch on Japanese attempts to establish an agricultural colony in Honduras for cultivating strategic crops.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Despatch 354: Erwin reports Japanese plans for a Honduran agricultural colony to grow cotton, sisal, and castor beans.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 354 regarding Japanese Colonization Scheme
